title: Buddy Petit's last jobs at Empire and his death
summary: Lewis tells how Petit played the last jobs at Empire, drank at a speakeasy, fell ill and was dead when the band returned.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I didn't go nice as far as the boy, then. But anyway, uh, tell me more about your last two jobs. You must have just played two jobs on the third day. He was a fan.
Well, he had been playing a little job off and on with that group of men, because, uh, it really wasn't an organized band.
But were you playing with this band down in that band?

I played with that band the whole tree nights at Empire. And, uh, when I came back that morning, but it was dead. Because he missed one of them nights. He took a ciggy. He went on across the right opposite. He was chasing. He had a speakeasy. And, uh, you went in that speakeasy and he'd done a lot of drinking. I mean.
This was an empire. No, no. He came from the last job. You mean the speakeasy was on St. Philip? On St. Philip, right. Opposite to the way he is. Yeah.

He went in there and he'd done a lot of drinking. And so, uh, he was sick, got sick. He had been sick anyway. And, uh, he couldn't make the last job. When we came in on the last job, he was dead. He died through that morning we left.
Well, how was he playing when he was playing at them, his last two nights? Well, he was playing pretty good.
He was, uh, he liked to sit up to the body of the year, you know, before, but he was playing pretty good.

So, uh, you were having a drink in there. So, you think it was the drinking man that killed him? Well, that was probably... Probably could have been, uh, cheating, killing, uh, or was such a kid. So, uh, how old was the man when he died?
Oh, he must have been at his farm, I'm sure. He grew up at the farm. Yes.
